statement: Let $f(x)=\dfrac{2x+1}{x-1}$ for $x\neq 1$. Find $f^{-1}(x)$, and verify that $f^{-1}(f(x))=x$ for all admissible $x$.
solution:
Set $y=\dfrac{2x+1}{x-1}$ and solve for $x$:
$$y(x-1)=2x+1 \;\Rightarrow\; yx-y=2x+1 \;\Rightarrow\; x(y-2)=y+1,$$
so $x=\dfrac{y+1}{y-2}$. Therefore
$$f^{-1}(x)=\frac{x+1}{x-2}\quad (x\neq 2).$$
Now verify:
$$f^{-1}(f(x))=\frac{f(x)+1}{f(x)-2}.$$
With $f(x)=\dfrac{2x+1}{x-1}$,
$$f(x)+1=\frac{2x+1}{x-1}+1=\frac{3x}{x-1},\qquad f(x)-2=\frac{2x+1}{x-1}-2=\frac{3}{x-1}.$$
Hence
$$f^{-1}(f(x))=\frac{\frac{3x}{x-1}}{\frac{3}{x-1}}=x,$$
as required.
hints: Swap x and y, then solve for y to get the inverse.
Compute f(x)+1 and f(x)-2 with a common denominator.
Divide the two expressions; the (x-1) cancels.
